title: “In My Skin,” Body Horror Cronenberg Can Only Dream Of

commenti.body: Aside from the didactic and reductive reading of Cronenberg, who most definitely does not present narratives where there is "a clear cause which can be overcome", this was an interesting write-up and provided me with two new films to add to my watchlist! Thanks :)
I would love to hear what you think of them. All I really meant to say about Cronenberg is that his films are not as rich or deep as these.

Not sure I would agree, but there is no real metric to accurately measure the "depth" of a film and we can only really speak to our own interpretations and experiences with then.

I would recommend revisiting Cronenberg if you have the inclination, particularly Dead Ringers and possibly Naked Lunch or The Fly. There is depth there for sure.

> In a Cronenberg film, there would be a clear cause that can be overcome. Body-horror films are often about a person’s body being invaded or changed by an outside force, but De Van's character is doing this to herself, for reasons we cannot see or understand. 
 
 
…What Cronenberg movies have you seen? This is one of the laziest takes I've read about a movie in a long time.
I think I've seen most of them. He's a good filmmaker, but films like The Fly and Scanners only go so far. In My Skin is much deeper, less sensationalized, and more substantive.

So two of his earliest body horror movies? Yep, those two where you could discribe it changed forced from the outside. Now do Videodrome, Crash, or eXistenZ. None of those could be considered to be 

Not that any of that equals depth though. You are just stating what you like about My Skin (and ignoring when Cronenberg does the same thing) and just claiming it to be deeper and more complex.


You can like something without needlessly putting other things down. If you are going to shit all over other work, at least say something substantive about them. But you can't.
 
 
The idea that "In a Cronenberg film, there would be a clear cause that can be overcome." is so ignorant that it makes me think you have absolutely nothing of value to say about cinema.
Have yo seen In My Skin? Or are you just being reactionary?

Lol choosing The Fly and Scanners as your examples kinda feels like cherry picking. I haven’t seen all of Cronenberg’s stuff, but those two are easily my least favorite and clearly his most commercial. Dead Ringers, Videodrome, and Crimes of the Future are all leagues above the depth of Scanners lol

I haven't, but I'm also not commenting about it. I am only talking about what you are saying about Cronenberg's movie, which is clearly and obviously incorrect. 

My Skin may have more depth and complexity than anything Cronenberg has made, but I can't judge that at this time. What I can judge is your absolutely braindead takes on Cronenberg's work.
>You are just stating what you like about My Skin (and ignoring when Cronenberg does the same thing)
Why do you have to be insulting? Can't you make your point without resorting to childish name calling?

Basing that off of what you wrote about In My Skin. 

Although given what you wrote about Cronenberg movies I probably shouldn't be taking your word on what is or isn't done in In My Skin.
I don't want to talk to you, you're too hostile. I'm here to talk about film not to be accosted.

Can't you make your point without shitting on other people's work?  I never called you names, just said your thoughts on Cronenberg's work were exceedingly stupid and lazy.

 Why is it okay for you to do that but not me? If you don't want negativity, don't bring it to the table. You are seemingly only able to talk about something you like by putting something else down, so why expect anything different from people responding to you?

Yah this not only reads like unnecessary shots at Cronenberg but also a complete lack of understanding or knowledge on the filmmaker’s work, philosophy, and commentary. How on earth does any of what OP mentioned fit Videodrome? 

No need to tear down one filmmaker’s entire body of work in order to hype this random French Extremity movie that has nothing to do with Cronenberg.
